key_insight: When checks can reliably expose failures but cannot prove correctness, learning only from verified negatives avoids rewarding false positives.
engineering_relevance: NOPO offers a training approach for code, logic, and math systems where partial checks are available but reliable correctness rewards are not.
method: Treat non-falsified responses as unlabeled rather than correct.
Suppress trusted verified negatives using a reference-relative loss.
Scale each group’s update by its proportion of non-falsified responses.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved pass@k over baselines across code, logic, and math benchmarks using unit-test, constraint-check, and LLM self-verifiers, with gains persisting under inference-time scaling and cross-benchmark transfer.
watch_item: NOPO depends on trustworthy negative judgments; erroneous failure labels could suppress correct solutions.
paper_title: Negative-Only Policy Optimization for One-Sided Verifiable Rewards
